items.title: Continuous singular simplex and real singular chain group
items.statement: For a topological space X, C_k(X;R) is the finite-support real vector space on maps Delta^k to X; zero for k<0.
items.proof_plan: For a topological space X, C_k(X;R) is the finite-support real vector space on maps Delta^k to X; zero for k<0. Identify Z[S_k] tensor_Z R with R[S_k] by [sigma] tensor r -> r[sigma], using the inverse on each supplied generator.

items.title: Real singular chain complex
items.statement: Boundary is the alternating sum of affine faces; d_0=0.
items.proof_plan: Boundary is the alternating sum of affine faces; d_0=0. The two occurrences of each codimension-two face have opposite signs. This verifies d squared equals zero over R and fixes the unaugmented convention.

items.title: Singular chains are covariantly functorial
items.statement: Send [sigma] to [f composed sigma] and extend R-linearly.
items.proof_plan: Send [sigma] to [f composed sigma] and extend R-linearly. Composition commutes with every face inclusion, hence with boundary. Identity and composition laws follow on generators.

items.proof_plan: Evaluation on [sigma] identifies Hom_R(R[S],R) and Hom_Z(Z[S],R) with all functions S->R; the inverse evaluates finite sums by sum r_sigma f(sigma). The two inverses and boundary compatibility are checked on generators, without choosing a vector-space basis.

items.title: Real singular cochain complex
items.statement: Define C^k=Hom_R(C_k,R), delta(phi)=phi composed boundary.
items.proof_plan: Define C^k=Hom_R(C_k,R), delta(phi)=phi composed boundary. Use the preceding explicit identification with Hom_Z(C_k(X;Z),R) to specialize AT-6; do not use Hom_Z(C_k(X;R),R). Delta squared vanishes by boundary squared.

items.proof_plan: Define H^k as ker(delta_k)/im(delta_(k-1)); inclusion of boundaries in cycles follows from delta squared. No identification with dual homology is part of this definition.

items.statement: For a supplied homotopy use its signed prism P, with dP+Pd=g_*-f_*.
items.proof_plan: For a supplied homotopy use its signed prism P, with dP+Pd=g_*-f_*. Precomposition gives a cochain homotopy, so cocycle pullbacks differ by a coboundary. Apply both inverse homotopies for a homotopy equivalence.

items.statement: For X=U union V open use i(c)=(-c,c), j(a,b)=a+b into the cover-small complex.
items.proof_plan: For X=U union V open use i(c)=(-c,c), j(a,b)=a+b into the cover-small complex. This differs from the published supplier by precomposing i with -1. Basis coefficients prove intersection=overlap, kernel=image, and surjectivity; both arrows commute with boundary.

items.title: Canonical extension by zero of a singular cochain on a simplex basis
items.statement: For overlap functional eta, define E_U eta on each U-simplex as eta(sigma) if its image lies in U intersect V, and zero otherwise, then extend linearly.
items.proof_plan: For overlap functional eta, define E_U eta on each U-simplex as eta(sigma) if its image lies in U intersect V, and zero otherwise, then extend linearly. This is canonical in classical ZF and is a degreewise section of restriction, not generally a cochain map.

items.statement: The first cochain term is Hom_R(C_*^{U,V},R).
items.proof_plan: The first cochain term is Hom_R(C_*^{U,V},R). Send a functional to its two restrictions and use (phi,psi)->psi|overlap-phi|overlap. Kernel pairs glue as functions on the union of bases. Surjectivity uses (-E_U eta,0). Only the sequence arrows, not that section, commute with delta.

items.proof_plan: A smooth simplex is a map on Delta^k that extends to an open neighbourhood in its k-dimensional affine span. Distinguish this from facewise smoothness. Boundaryless targets are supplied by DG-7; the extension-into-boundary-target case remains an explicit scope question.

items.statement: Take finite real sums of smooth simplices, boundary the same signed face sum, and the R-linear dual for cochains.
items.proof_plan: Take finite real sums of smooth simplices, boundary the same signed face sum, and the R-linear dual for cochains. Affine face maps pull an open extension back to an open neighbourhood of the face; thus it is a subcomplex. Define its cohomology by cycles modulo boundaries.

items.proof_plan: Postcompose smooth simplices with a smooth map and restrict extension neighbourhoods if necessary. Face commutation gives a chain map; duality gives contravariant cochains and cohomology. Identity and composition hold on each generator.

items.statement: Subdivision and its subdivision homotopy compose with affine simplex maps, so preserve smooth chains.
items.proof_plan: Subdivision and its subdivision homotopy compose with affine simplex maps, so preserve smooth chains. A homotopy prism preserves smooth chains only when the supplied homotopy is smooth; arbitrary continuous homotopies do not qualify. Check the extension near each compact prism simplex.

items.title: Smooth singular mayer vietoris sequence
items.statement: Repeat the least subdivision depth recursion inside smooth chains: m(sigma)=max of its least small depth and the face depths; D sigma=sum_{i<m(sigma)} T S^i sigma; r=1-dD-Dd.
items.proof_plan: Repeat the least subdivision depth recursion inside smooth chains: m(sigma)=max of its least small depth and the face depths; D sigma=sum_{i<m(sigma)} T S^i sigma; r=1-dD-Dd. Each correction on a face starts at that face depth and is small and smooth. Then repeat the basis SES and degreewise zero extension, followed by the LES. This proves smooth MV independently of the comparison theorem.

items.title: Compatible smooth simplex faces have a neighbourhood extension
items.statement: For a boundaryless target, compatible smooth maps on the faces of a simplex locally extend near their union.
items.proof_plan: For a boundaryless target, compatible smooth maps on the faces of a simplex locally extend near their union. Near a point omit a barycentric coordinate that is positive; incident faces become coordinate hyperplanes. In a target chart inductively correct an extension F by F-F composed projection_j+F_j composed projection_j. Compatibility on intersections preserves prior faces; restrict neighbourhoods so the image stays in the target chart. Global neighbourhood extension uses an embedding, a finite partition on the compact boundary and tubular retraction. The supplied relative Whitney theorem assumes smoothness on a neighbourhood, so this missing bridge must precede its use. Audit that global extension and boundary-target variant before readiness.

items.title: Relative smoothing of a continuous simplex along its faces
items.statement: Prescribed face smoothings require compatible homotopies from the original faces, not merely arbitrary new face maps.
items.proof_plan: Prescribed face smoothings require compatible homotopies from the original faces, not merely arbitrary new face maps. Extend the homotopy from bottom plus sides of Delta times I by the explicit radial retraction from (barycentre,2). At the top use the local face-extension lemma, an embedded-target retraction and a cutoff to make the top map smooth near the boundary. Apply relative Whitney on an open neighbourhood in affine space, fixed near the boundary. Delay this last homotopy by a continuous u(x)<1 in the interior with u=1 at the boundary, so prescribed face homotopies keep their original time. Compactness proves continuity at boundary time 1. AC_omega is inherited from Whitney; no selection over all simplices. Collar/extension details and boundary targets remain held for review.

items.title: Smooth singular chains compute singular homology
items.statement: For each particular cycle, take its finite support and all iterated faces and perform the relative smoothing induction on distinct maps, so repeated faces receive identical choices.
items.proof_plan: For each particular cycle, take its finite support and all iterated faces and perform the relative smoothing induction on distinct maps, so repeated faces receive identical choices. The prism identity shows the cycle homologous to its smooth image. For injectivity start with a finite bounding chain and fix its already-smooth faces; its smoothed boundary is the original smooth cycle. No globally selected smoothing operator is asserted.

items.title: Smooth continuous singular cohomology comparison is an isomorphism on convex coordinate domains
items.statement: In a nonempty convex coordinate domain fix one point and use the smooth affine contraction.
items.proof_plan: In a nonempty convex coordinate domain fix one point and use the smooth affine contraction. Both prism homotopies identify cohomology with that of a point: R in degree zero, zero in higher degrees. The restriction map at a point is the identity, so naturality gives the comparison isomorphism. Empty domains give zero complexes. For boundary charts use convex half-boxes only after their extension convention is resolved.

items.title: De rham and singular cohomology respect countable disjoint unions
items.statement: For a supplied countable disjoint family every simplex has connected domain and lies in one component; chains are a direct sum, cochains a product.
items.proof_plan: For a supplied countable disjoint family every simplex has connected domain and lies in one component; chains are a direct sum, cochains a product. Smooth forms are likewise products by local smoothness. Kernels are products without choice; under AC_omega choose one primitive for each component boundary to obtain image(delta)=product image(delta_i). Therefore H(product)=product H, naturally. State AC_omega and identify this exact choice use, not full injectivity of R.

items.title: Countable mayer vietoris open set principle
items.statement: Required open-set principle: a natural cohomology comparison commuting with two-open MV and countable disjoint unions, and an isomorphism on rational boxes, is an isomorphism on manifolds with a supplied countable coordinate cover.
items.proof_plan: Required open-set principle: a natural cohomology comparison commuting with two-open MV and countable disjoint unions, and an isomorphism on rational boxes, is an isomorphism on manifolds with a supplied countable coordinate cover. Finite unions follow from MV and five lemma, using intersections. For increasing unions one must construct the exhaustion bands, prove the odd/even disjoint decomposition and verify their overlaps are already in the class. Then first apply this to Euclidean opens and only afterwards to finite intersections of manifold charts. Exact exhaustion/band proof and a complete authoritative source remain unresolved; do not replace this by an unjustified direct-limit assertion.

items.title: Connection on a smooth vector bundle
items.statement: For a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle E on M, a connection is an R-linear operator Gamma(E)->Gamma(T*M tensor E) with nabla(fs)=df tensor s+f nabla(s).

items.title: A bundle connection is local and restricts to open sets
items.statement: If s vanishes near p choose a bump chi supported there with chi(p)=1.
items.proof_plan: If s vanishes near p choose a bump chi supported there with chi(p)=1. From 0=nabla_X(chi s)(p)=Xchi(p)s(p)+chi(p)nabla_Xs(p) infer nabla_Xs(p)=0; no derivative-zero strengthening of the bump statement is needed. Multiply a local section by a bump equal to one on a smaller neighbourhood (supplied by the chart-bump proof) and extend by zero. The vanishing argument makes the restricted derivative independent of extension; local formulas give smoothness and uniqueness. Directional dependence only on X(p) follows directly from evaluating the E-valued one-form.

items.statement: Subtract the two Leibniz formulas: the df term cancels.
items.proof_plan: Subtract the two Leibniz formulas: the df term cancels. The difference is C-infinity-linear in both X and s. In a frame its smooth matrix is omega_1-omega_0 and transforms homogeneously, hence defines an End(E)-valued one-form. Do not infer fibrewise dependence from linearity without locality/local-frame verification.

items.title: Every smooth vector bundle admits a connection
items.statement: Assume AC. Every finite-rank smooth real vector bundle over a smooth manifold, with boundary allowed, admits a smooth connection.
items.proof_plan: Use full AC explicitly for the arbitrary indexed choices in the published subordinate-coordinate-ball/shrinking route and for the choices of local frames and bump data. The published partition argument is used with that stronger assumption, not as a proof of its advertised AC_omega bound. Choose a locally finite smooth partition (rho_i) subordinate to bundle trivializations and the flat derivative nabla^(i) in each chosen frame. For a section s, extend rho_i nabla^(i)s by zero; this is smooth since the support of rho_i lies inside its trivializing open set. The locally finite sum defines a smooth E-valued one-form operator. R-linearity is immediate, and the Leibniz rule is sum_i rho_i (df tensor s+f nabla^(i)s)=df tensor s+f nabla s because sum_i rho_i=1. The weights multiply derivatives and are not differentiated. This proves existence, not canonicity or a minimal choice bound. Results that start with a given connection do not inherit this existence assumption.

items.title: Torsion free means curvature free
items.statement: For an affine connection put R(X,Y)Z=nabla_X nabla_Y Z-nabla_Y nabla_X Z-nabla_[X,Y] Z; curvature-free here means R=0. The assertion that torsion-free implies curvature-free is false, even for a Levi–Civita connection on the plane.
items.proof_plan: First supply the local meaning and invariance of R, rather than cite the later DG-21 curvature theory. The displayed commutator uses intrinsic covariant derivatives and the Lie bracket. In R(fX,Y)Z, the -(Yf)nabla_X Z from differentiating f cancels the +(Yf)nabla_X Z from [fX,Y]=f[X,Y]-(Yf)X; hence it equals fR(X,Y)Z. Skew symmetry gives linearity in Y. Expanding the two iterated derivatives on fZ gives second-derivative term (X(Yf)-Y(Xf))Z=[X,Y](f)Z, canceled by the bracket derivative, while the two cross first-derivative terms cancel pairwise. Thus R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z. Additivity and real linearity follow from the connection laws. In local smooth frames these identities express R through smooth coefficients and pointwise components of X,Y,Z, so it is an intrinsic smooth tensor and its vanishing is frame-independent. Now take g=exp(2x^2)(dx^2+dy^2) on R^2. Its Levi–Civita coefficients from the preceding formula are Gamma^x_xx=2x, Gamma^x_yy=-2x, Gamma^y_xy=Gamma^y_yx=2x, and the other coefficients are zero. They are symmetric in the lower indices, so torsion vanishes. Since coordinate fields commute, nabla_x nabla_y partial_y=(-2-4x^2)partial_x, whereas nabla_y nabla_x partial_y=-4x^2 partial_x. Consequently R(partial_x,partial_y)partial_y=-2partial_x, in particular nonzero at x=0. No Gauss–Bonnet, holonomy theorem, Bianchi identity or later curvature supplier is used; DG-21 retains the full curvature development.

items.title: A connection one form on a trivial line bundle
items.statement: For a smooth one-form a on M, the rule nabla s=ds+a s defines a line-bundle connection in its global frame.
items.proof_plan: For a smooth one-form a on M, the rule nabla s=ds+a s defines a line-bundle connection in its global frame. Choosing a=x dy on R^2 gives a concrete nontrivial coefficient.

items.title: Gauge transformation of a connection one form
items.statement: On a real line bundle change frame eprime=e exp(f).
items.proof_plan: On a real line bundle change frame eprime=e exp(f). Then Aprime formula gives omegaPrime=omega+df; for omega=0,f=x the new coefficient is dx although the intrinsic connection is unchanged.

items.title: Pullback of the flat connection
items.statement: Pull back the constant frame and zero connection matrix of a trivial bundle along f:N->M; f*0=0, so the pulled-back connection is the componentwise derivative in that pulled-back frame..
items.proof_plan: Pull back the constant frame and zero connection matrix of a trivial bundle along f:N->M; f*0=0, so the pulled-back connection is the componentwise derivative in that pulled-back frame.

items.title: Parallel transport for a scalar linear ode
items.statement: Solve vprime=-a(t)v: v(b)=exp(-integral_a^b a(t)dt)v(a).
items.proof_plan: Solve vprime=-a(t)v: v(b)=exp(-integral_a^b a(t)dt)v(a). Verify the derivative and initial condition; zero input gives zero and reversal changes the exponent sign.

items.title: The euclidean levi civita connection
items.statement: For Euclidean coordinates g_ij=delta_ij all derivatives of g vanish, so every Christoffel symbol is zero and parallel vectors have constant components..

items.title: Christoffel symbols in polar coordinates
items.statement: For g=dr^2+r^2 dtheta^2 on r>0 obtain Gamma^r_theta theta=-r and Gamma^theta_r theta=Gamma^theta_theta r=1/r, all others zero.
items.proof_plan: For g=dr^2+r^2 dtheta^2 on r>0 obtain Gamma^r_theta theta=-r and Gamma^theta_r theta=Gamma^theta_theta r=1/r, all others zero. State the chart excludes r=0.

items.title: Levi civita connection of a conformal plane metric
items.statement: For g=exp(2u)(dx^2+dy^2), substitute into Christoffels to get Gamma^k_ij=delta^k_j u_i+delta^k_i u_j-delta_ij u_k.
items.proof_plan: For g=exp(2u)(dx^2+dy^2), substitute into Christoffels to get Gamma^k_ij=delta^k_j u_i+delta^k_i u_j-delta_ij u_k. Give u=x^2 as a nonconstant smooth example.

items.title: Parallel transport on the round sphere along the equator
items.statement: On the unit sphere the projected ambient derivative nabla_XY=D_XY+<X,Y>p is tangent, compatible and torsion free; Levi-Civita uniqueness identifies it.
items.proof_plan: On the unit sphere the projected ambient derivative nabla_XY=D_XY+<X,Y>p is tangent, compatible and torsion free; Levi-Civita uniqueness identifies it. Along gamma(t)=(cos t,sin t,0), the tangent (-sin t,cos t,0) and constant (0,0,1) are parallel, so full equatorial-loop transport is the identity.

items.title: A torsion free connection that is not metric compatible
items.statement: On R with g=dx^2 take Gamma^1_11=1.
items.proof_plan: On R with g=dx^2 take Gamma^1_11=1. Torsion vanishes in dimension one, while compatibility fails since partial_x g(1,1)=0 and the derivative RHS is 2. No claim that this connection is incompatible with every possible metric.

items.title: Path dependent parallel transport on the sphere
items.statement: Compute the same projected connection on the three quarter great circles from e1 to e2 to e3 to e1.
items.proof_plan: Compute the same projected connection on the three quarter great circles from e1 to e2 to e3 to e1. Along each arc its tangent and fixed normal are parallel. Starting vector e2 ends as e3 at e1; the constant loop fixes e2. This is explicit path dependence, without Gauss-Bonnet or a curvature/holonomy theorem.

items.title: Hessian and divergence in euclidean coordinates
items.statement: Euclidean g has zero Christoffels.
items.proof_plan: Euclidean g has zero Christoffels. Hence Hess f has entries partial_i partial_j f and div X=sum_i partial_i X^i. For f=x^2 y in R^2, Hess=[[2y,2x],[2x,0]], and X=(x^2,xy) has divergence 3x.
